questions.questionText: A pipe fills a tank in 5 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom, it takes 7 hours to fill the tank. In how many hours will the leak alone empty the full tank?
questions.explanation: Leak rate = 1/5 - 1/7 = 2/35 per hour. Time to empty = 17.5 hours.

questions.questionText: A tank is 1/3 full. A pipe can fill a full tank in 18 minutes and an outlet can empty a full tank in 24 minutes. If both are opened, how long will it take to fill the tank completely?

questions.questionText: Pipes A and B fill a tank in 45 and 12 minutes and pipe C empties it in 24 minutes. They are opened one after another for one minute each in the order A, B, C and the sequence repeats. In how many minutes will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 360 units: A adds 8, B adds 30, C removes 15 per minute. One 3-minute cycle gives 23. Tracking the cycles minute by minute, the tank is exactly full at the end of minute 44.
questions.shortcut: Net per cycle, then simulate the final cycle.

questions.questionText: Two pipes deliver 75 litres and 30 litres per minute into a tank of capacity 1050 litres. How long will they take to fill the empty tank when working together?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 75 + 30 = 105 litres/min. Time = 1050/105 = 10 minutes.
questions.shortcut: Time = capacity / (sum of the flow rates).

questions.questionText: Pipe A can fill a tank in 9 minutes and pipe B in 15 minutes. If both are opened together, what is the ratio of the water delivered by A to that delivered by B?
questions.explanation: Delivery is proportional to rate. A : B = 1/9 : 1/15 = 15 : 9 = 5:3.
questions.shortcut: In the same time the volumes are in the ratio of the rates, i.e. the inverse of the times.

questions.questionText: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 60 and 24 minutes respectively. They are opened together. What fraction of the tank is still empty after 3 minutes?
questions.explanation: Both fill 7/120 per minute, so in 3 minutes they fill 7/40. Empty fraction = 1 - 7/40 = 33/40.
questions.shortcut: Add the rates, multiply by time, subtract from 1.

questions.questionText: A pipe can fill a tank in 8 minutes and another pipe can empty it in 10 minutes. If both are opened together, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/8 - 1/10 = 1/40 per minute. Time = 40 minutes.
questions.shortcut: Filling and emptying: time = (a x c)/(c - a) = (8 x 10)/2.

questions.questionText: A pipe fills a tank in 10 minutes and an outlet empties it in 40 minutes. They are opened alternately for one minute each, the inlet first. In how many minutes will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Capacity = 40 units. Inlet adds 4 and outlet removes 1 per minute. Net per 2-minute cycle = 3. Following the cycles, the tank is exactly full at the end of minute 25.
questions.shortcut: Compute the net gain per cycle; check the last partial cycle step by step.

questions.questionText: Two pipes can fill a tank in 15 and 20 hours respectively. When both are open, a leak makes them take 10 hours instead. In how many hours would the leak alone empty a full tank?
questions.explanation: Without the leak the rate is 1/15 + 1/20 = 7/60. With the leak it is 1/10. Leak rate = 7/60 - 1/10 = 1/60, so it empties the tank in 60 hours.
questions.shortcut: Leak rate = (rate without leak) - (rate with leak).

questions.questionText: A pipe can fill a tank in 6 minutes and another pipe can empty it in 8 minutes. If both are opened together, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/6 - 1/8 = 1/24 per minute. Time = 24 minutes.
questions.shortcut: Filling and emptying: time = (a x c)/(c - a) = (6 x 8)/2.

questions.questionText: A pipe fills a tank at 100 litres per minute while a leak drains 10 litres per minute. The empty tank is filled in 12 minutes. What is the capacity of the tank?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 100 - 10 = 90 litres/min. Capacity = 90 x 12 = 1080 litres.
questions.shortcut: Use the net flow rate (inflow - leak) x time.

questions.questionText: A tank is filled by a pipe in 9 hours, and a leak can empty the full tank in 15 hours. If both the pipe and the leak are working, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/9 - 1/15 = 2/45 per hour. Time = 22.5 hours.
questions.shortcut: Time with the leak = (fill time x leak time)/(leak time - fill time).

questions.questionText: A tank is filled by a pipe in 4 hours, and a leak can empty the full tank in 12 hours. If both the pipe and the leak are working, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/4 - 1/12 = 1/6 per hour. Time = 6 hours.
questions.shortcut: Time with the leak = (fill time x leak time)/(leak time - fill time).

questions.questionText: A pipe fills a tank at 40 litres per minute while a leak drains 25 litres per minute. The empty tank is filled in 15 minutes. What is the capacity of the tank?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 40 - 25 = 15 litres/min. Capacity = 15 x 15 = 225 litres.
questions.shortcut: Use the net flow rate (inflow - leak) x time.

questions.questionText: Two pipes can fill a tank in 30 and 48 minutes, and a third pipe can empty it in 20 minutes. If all three are opened together, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/30 + 1/48 - 1/20 = 1/240 per minute. Time = 240 minutes.
questions.shortcut: Filling rates add; emptying rates subtract.

questions.questionText: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 24, 20 and 30 minutes respectively. How long will the tank take to fill if all three are opened together?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/24 + 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/8 per minute. Time = 8 minutes.
questions.shortcut: Add the three fill rates and take the reciprocal.

questions.questionText: Two pipes can fill a tank in 48 and 40 minutes, and a third pipe can empty it in 30 minutes. If all three are opened together, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/48 + 1/40 - 1/30 = 1/80 per minute. Time = 80 minutes.
questions.shortcut: Filling rates add; emptying rates subtract.

questions.questionText: A pipe can fill a tank in 20 minutes and another pipe can empty it in 24 minutes. If both are opened together, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/20 - 1/24 = 1/120 per minute. Time = 120 minutes.
questions.shortcut: Filling and emptying: time = (a x c)/(c - a) = (20 x 24)/4.

questions.questionText: A pipe fills a tank in 10 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom, it takes 14 hours to fill the tank. In how many hours will the leak alone empty the full tank?
questions.explanation: Leak rate = 1/10 - 1/14 = 1/35 per hour. Time to empty = 35 hours.
questions.shortcut: Leak time = (a x b)/(b - a) = (10 x 14)/4.

questions.questionText: A pipe fills a tank at 40 litres per minute while a leak drains 25 litres per minute. The empty tank is filled in 20 minutes. What is the capacity of the tank?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 40 - 25 = 15 litres/min. Capacity = 15 x 20 = 300 litres.
questions.shortcut: Use the net flow rate (inflow - leak) x time.

questions.questionText: A pipe can fill a tank in 60 minutes. What fraction of the tank is filled after 50 minutes?
questions.explanation: Fraction filled in 50 minutes = 50/60 = 5/6.
questions.shortcut: Fraction filled = time elapsed / total time.

questions.questionText: A tank is filled by a pipe in 4 hours, and a leak can empty the full tank in 8 hours. If both the pipe and the leak are working, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/4 - 1/8 = 1/8 per hour. Time = 8 hours.
questions.shortcut: Time with the leak = (fill time x leak time)/(leak time - fill time).

questions.questionText: Two pipes can fill a tank in 10 and 15 minutes, and a third pipe can empty it in 18 minutes. If all three are opened together, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/10 + 1/15 - 1/18 = 1/9 per minute. Time = 9 minutes.
questions.shortcut: Filling rates add; emptying rates subtract.

questions.questionText: A tank is filled by a pipe in 2 hours, and a leak can empty the full tank in 4 hours. If both the pipe and the leak are working, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/2 - 1/4 = 1/4 per hour. Time = 4 hours.
questions.shortcut: Time with the leak = (fill time x leak time)/(leak time - fill time).

questions.questionText: Pipe A can fill a tank in 10 minutes and pipe B in 6 minutes. If both are opened together, what is the ratio of the water delivered by A to that delivered by B?
questions.explanation: Delivery is proportional to rate. A : B = 1/10 : 1/6 = 6 : 10 = 3:5.
questions.shortcut: In the same time the volumes are in the ratio of the rates, i.e. the inverse of the times.

questions.questionText: Pipe A fills a tank in 30 minutes and pipe B in 12 minutes. A is opened first, and B is opened 2 minutes later. In how many minutes from the start is the tank full?
questions.explanation: A alone fills 2/30 in 2 minutes. Remaining = 14/15. Together they fill 7/60 per minute, so 8 more minutes. Total = 10 minutes.
questions.shortcut: Time from the start = head-start time + time with both pipes.
